{{Short description|Result about the connection between projective planes and spheres}}
In [[projective geometry]] in mathematics, the '''Arnold–Kuiper–Massey theorem''' (or '''AKM theorem''') includes three connected results about [[Projective plane|projective planes]] and their connection to [[N-sphere|spheres]]. The Arnold–Kuiper–Massey theorem is named after [[Vladimir Arnold]], [[Nicolaas Kuiper]] und William Massey, who described its complex version in 1971, 1974 and 1973, respectively. The quaternionic generalization was described by Vladimir Arnold in 1999 as well as by [[Michael Atiyah]] and [[Edward Witten]] in 2001. The octonionic generalization was described by Michael Atiyah and Jürgen Berndt in 2002.

== Complex AKM theorem ==
The first [[orthogonal group]] <math>\operatorname{O}(1)\cong S^0=\{-1,+1\}\subsetneq\mathbb{R}</math> of unit real numbers acts on the [[complex projective space]] <math>\mathbb{C}P^n</math> by [[Complex conjugate|complex conjugation]]. For the complex projective plane, the [[Quotient space (topology)|quotient space]] is [[Homeomorphism|homeomorphic]] to a [[sphere]]:<ref>Massey 1973, p. 371</ref><ref name=":1">Atiyah & Berndt 2003, Eq. (1.1)</ref>

: <math>\mathbb{C}P^2/\operatorname{O}(1)
\cong S^4.</math>

== Quaternionic AKM theorem ==
The first [[unitary group]] <math>\operatorname{U}(1)\cong S^1\subsetneq\mathbb{C}</math> of [[unit complex numbers]] acts on the imaginary components of the [[quaternionic projective space]] <math>\mathbb{H}P^n</math> by multiplication. For the quaternionic projective plane, the quotient space is homeomorphic to a sphere:<ref>Atiyah & Witten 2001, Eq. (5.50)</ref><ref name=":1" />

: <math>\mathbb{H}P^2/\operatorname{U}(1)
\cong S^7.</math>

== Octonionic AKM theorem ==
The first [[symplectic group]] <math>\operatorname{Sp}(1)\cong S^3\subsetneq\mathbb{H}</math> of [[unit quaternions]] acts on the second octonionic projective space or [[Cayley plane]] <math>\mathbb{O}P^2</math> (there is no <math>\mathbb{O}P^n</math> for <math>n\geq 3</math> due to the octonions not being [[Associative property|associative]]) with:<ref name=":1" />

: <math>\mathbb{O}P^2/\operatorname{Sp}(1)
\cong S^{13}.</math>
